args.body:
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM

TO: Northgale deal team / Transaction Committee
FROM: Harrow & Vane LLP — Energy, Natural Resources & Project Development Group
RE: TxDOT Concession Agreement — Counterparty Markup Review
DATE: [Engagement Date]
STATUS: Privileged & Confidential — Attorney Work Product

I. SCOPE AND MATERIALS REVIEWED

We have been engaged to compare the counterparty markup of the Texas Department of Transportation ("TxDOT" or the "Counterparty") against our client's original draft and the negotiation playbook, and to cross-reference the lender and surety letters plus the financial model. This memorandum identifies every deviation introduced by the TxDOT markup, reconciles each deviation against the base materials, assigns risk ratings, and sets out recommended counter-proposal language.

Materials reviewed for this memo:
- Original draft of the Concession Agreement (our client's base form) and the underlying deal materials (Matter File 13).
- TxDOT markup of the Concession Agreement (the operative counter-draft).
- Disclosure Schedules and Exhibits (schedules/exhibits to the Concession Agreement).
- Deal team correspondence reflecting the controlling negotiation priorities.
- Cross-reference materials: lender letter, surety letter, and financial model, as reflected in and reconciled through the schedules and exhibits.

For avoidance of doubt, an unrelated administrative correspondence file (File 13) was misfiled into the matter folder and concerns a different engagement. It has been disregarded and must not be relied upon for this analysis.

II. OVERALL ASSESSMENT

The TxDOT markup accepts most firm-standard provisions of the Concession Agreement. However, it introduces three material deviations that must be reconciled against the base materials: (1) a reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket; (2) expansion of the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") definition to add carve-outs for regulatory action; and (3) shortening of the survival period for the core representations. Each is addressed below.

Controlling deal-team instruction: The latest partnership email revises the client's priorities. The client will concede the basket conversion, but treats any reduction of the survival period as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages that stated the opposite ordering are superseded and do not control. The recommendations below reflect the controlling instruction only.

III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification cap reduction and basket conversion (deductible → tipping)

Description. The TxDOT markup silently reduces the indemnification cap and converts the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

Reconciliation against base materials and related materials. The original draft provides for a fixed indemnification cap and a single deductible basket. The reduced cap, combined with a tipping basket, increases the client's net indemnity exposure at the margin: with a tipping basket, once the basket threshold is crossed the Counterparty recovers the entire claim amount (including amounts below the basket), whereas a deductible requires the Counterparty to bear the first tranche. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift back to the client, exacerbating the exposure. Under the controlling deal-team instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion (i.e., accept the tipping basket) but should resist any reduction of the indemnification cap.

Risk rating. MEDIUM-HIGH — the cap reduction is value-shifting and must be resisted or offset; the basket conversion is an acceptable concession per deal-team direction.

Counter-proposal language.

"Notwithstanding anything in [the markup], Section __ (Indemnification Cap) is revised to provide that the aggregate liability of [the Concessionaire] for indemnification claims shall not exceed (i) 15% of the total project consideration, as set forth in the financial model, or (ii) the amount of the performance bond and payment bond posted under the surety letter, whichever is greater. The parties acknowledge the basket shall operate as a tipping basket: once the aggregate amount of losses exceeds the basket threshold of $____, [the Counterparty] may recover the full amount of all losses, including those below the threshold."

We recommend retaining the cap at the original draft level. Should the Counterparty insist on a cap reduction, any such reduction must be mirrored against the retained liabilities in Schedule 5.2 and must not erode the security afforded by the lender and surety package reflected in the financial model.

DEVIATION 2 — MAE definition: new carve-outs for regulatory action

Description. The TxDOT markup adds to the definition of Material Adverse Effect carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue in this matter.

Reconciliation against base materials and schedules. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect precisely the regulatory-action carve-outs the markup seeks to introduce. Adding broad carve-outs for "regulatory action" would, in substance, strip out the very MAE events disclosed in Schedule 3.7 and would transfer the regulatory risk to the client. This is inconsistent with the original draft's MAE definition, which did not carve out such action, and is inconsistent with the risk allocation reflected in the lender letter, the surety letter, and the financial model (all of which price in the disclosed regulatory exposure).

Risk rating. HIGH — if accepted unmodified, the client would bear unallocated regulatory and cost risk inconsistent with the deal fundamentals and the disclosed schedule.

Counter-proposal language.

"The definition of Material Adverse Effect in Section __ is amended to include a carve-out for governmental or regulatory action only to the extent such action (a) applies generally to the relevant industry and does not discriminate against the Concessionaire, and (b) does not arise from, or relate to, the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7. No MAE carve-out shall exclude any existing regulatory proceedings disclosed on Schedule 3.7, and any such proceeding shall continue to constitute an MAE event to the extent it has a material adverse effect on the Project as defined in the financial model."

DEVIATION 3 — Survival period shortened for core representations

Description. The TxDOT markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations.

Reconciliation against base materials and exhibits. Exhibit B to the Concession Agreement sets the survival matrix. The markup's shortened limitation period directly contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B. The schedules state that the scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials. Under the controlling deal-team instruction, any reduction of the survival period is a walk-away issue for the client and must be rejected as a threshold, non-negotiable item.

Risk rating. SEVERE / WALK-AWAY — the deal team has directed that any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue; this deviation therefore cannot be accepted.

Counter-proposal language.

"The survival periods for the representations and warranties set forth in Exhibit B shall remain unmodified. The parties agree that the survival of the fundamental representations, the tax representations, and the environmental representations shall be the longer of the applicable statutory limitation period or the periods set forth in Exhibit B. Any surviving claims shall be governed by the survival matrix in Exhibit B, and no provision of this Agreement shall be construed to shorten those periods."

IV. CROSS-REFERENCE TO LENDER AND SURETY LETTERS AND FINANCIAL MODEL

The deviations in the TxDOT markup, if accepted, would collectively erode the security and risk allocation that underpin the financing and bonding structure:

- Lender letter. The indemnification cap reduction and MAE carve-outs would allocate to the Concessionaire risks for which the lender has conditioned disbursement. The financial model assumes a stable indemnity profile; any erosion triggers a potential default or funding condition failure.
- Surety letter. The surety's performance and payment bonds are sized to the disclosed regulatory exposure (Schedule 3.7) and retained liabilities (Schedule 5.2). Accepting the cap reduction or the regulatory MAE carve-outs would undermine the basis for surety coverage and could render the bonds inadequate.
- Financial model. The model prices the indemnity cap, basket, MAE exposure, and survival periods. Each deviation must be tested against the model before acceptance; the counter-proposal language above is designed to keep the risk profile consistent with the model.

V. RISK-RATING SUMMARY

1. Indemnification cap reduction — MEDIUM-HIGH — resist cap reduction; concede tipping basket per deal-team direction.
2. MAE regulatory-action carve-outs — HIGH — reject as drafted; limit to general, non-discriminatory regulatory action excluding disclosed Schedule 3.7 inquiries.
3. Survival-period reduction for core representations — SEVERE / WALK-AWAY — reject; cannot accept per controlling deal-team instruction.

VI. RECOMMENDED COURSE OF ACTION

1. Concede the basket conversion (tipping basket) consistent with deal-team direction.
2. Reject the indemnification cap reduction; if forced to move, tie any cap reduction to Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities and the surety/lender security package.
3. Reject the MAE regulatory carve-outs as drafted; counter with the narrow, non-discriminatory carve-out that preserves Schedule 3.7 exposure and the financial model's risk allocation.
4. Refuse any survival-period reduction; this is the client's walk-away item.

VII. CONCLUSION

Prepare to transmit the counter-proposal language set forth above to TxDOT counsel. Confirm with the deal team prior to conceding any further point beyond the agreed basket conversion. The survival-period reduction remains the non-negotiable floor for this transaction.

Prepared by: Harrow & Vane LLP
